evidence: src/controllers/cardsController.ts: create, activate, getStatement, blockCard, unblockCard and createVirtual each delegate to one cardServices method and respond.
src/controllers/paymentsController.ts: buyOnPointOfSale and buyOnline delegate to paymentServices.insertPayment and insertOnlinePayment, with no business logic in the handlers.
src/controllers/rechargeController.ts: recharge delegates to rechargeService.recharge(cardId, amount) and responds with 200.
Only src/controllers/cardsController.ts getStatement calls parseInt(cardId). This is request-parameter coercion, not a duplicated rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three controllers serve one concern: thin Express handlers that read the request, call a single service, and send the HTTP response. Each controller maps to one service (cardServices, paymentServices, rechargeService). Nothing bypasses those services, and no business rules or invariants are duplicated across the files. The handlers share one pattern (destructure the request, await the service call, respond with 200 or 201). Two small inconsistencies exist. paymentsController types the request body with interfaces while the other controllers destructure untyped req.body. Only getStatement parses a route param. Neither splits the module's concerns. The incoming imports of BuyOnPOSBody and BuyOnlineBody from services and schemas are a dependency-direction matter, which is out of scope.
